anchors.task: Professor Ortiz asks whether universities should require every student to take a course in personal finance. Ana says budgeting is learned at home; Ben says a short online module is enough.
anchors.text: I believe a required personal finance course is worth the credit hours, and I disagree with Ana that home is enough. Many students, including my own roommates, grew up in families that never discussed credit scores or loans, so they arrive at university making expensive mistakes with their first credit card. A full course could do what Ben's short module cannot: students would practise with real scenarios, such as comparing two rental contracts or calculating the true cost of a student loan over ten years. Because these decisions shape the rest of their lives, universities have a responsibility to teach them as seriously as they teach writing or statistics.
anchors.reason: Clear position, new argument beyond both posts, well-developed example, precise vocabulary and varied sentences with almost no errors.

anchors.task: Professor Ortiz asks whether universities should require every student to take a course in personal finance. Ana says budgeting is learned at home; Ben says a short online module is enough.
anchors.text: I think universities should require a finance course, although it does not need to be long. Ana is right that some families teach budgeting, but many students never had this chance, so the university should make sure everyone has the same basic knowledge. In my experience, the most useful topics would be loans and saving, because these are the areas where young people make the biggest mistakes. A course with a teacher also gives students a chance to ask about their own situation, which is not possible in an online module like the one Ben suggests.
anchors.reason: Relevant and clear contribution with adequate development; good range, a few awkward phrases and minor errors.

anchors.task: You borrowed a camera from your friend Sam for a trip, and it was damaged. Write an email to Sam: explain what happened, apologize, and suggest how you will fix the situation.
anchors.text:
Hi Sam,

I am afraid I have some bad news about your camera. On the last day of the trip, a sudden gust of wind knocked it off the table at our campsite, and the lens cap and the zoom ring were cracked. I feel terrible, because I know how carefully you look after your equipment.

I would like to make this right. I have already found a repair shop near campus that can replace both parts by Friday, and I will cover the full cost. If you would rather have a new lens, just tell me and I will order one instead.

Again, I am really sorry.

Best,
Jordan
anchors.reason: All three points fully covered with detail, natural friendly register, clear organization and accurate language.
